label: Gerard: GLP-1 analogue with confirmed malnutrition
title: GLP-1 analogue with confirmed malnutrition
statement: It is necessary to review and optimize the prescription of a GLP-1 analogue in a patient with a confirmed diagnosis of malnutrition.

plain_summary: A confirmed diagnosis of malnutrition during GLP-1 analogue treatment calls for review at any BMI.

medicine_groups.name: GLP-1 analogues
medicine_groups.note: Xultophy contains liraglutide with insulin degludec. Soliqua contains lixisenatide with insulin glargine. Count a listed ingredient in a combination or a generic pack labelled with its ingredient and company name. Exclude dual GIP/GLP-1 agonists.

rule_for_models: For a GLP-1 analogue supply, cite the supply, the recorded type 2 diabetes, the evidence that the medicine is used for diabetes and the confirmed diagnosis of malnutrition during treatment. If a required fact is missing and the other evidence fits, report a possible finding, name each missing fact and ask what the medicine was prescribed for if the reason is unknown. Give no finding if the medicine is used only for a reason other than type 2 diabetes, the recorded diabetes type is outside the criterion or malnutrition is excluded.
cannot_be_seen: Weight loss, a low BMI or a nutritional supplement alone cannot establish the diagnosis.
ask_the_gp: Could you confirm whether malnutrition was diagnosed during this treatment and, if so, review the suitability of the GLP-1 analogue?

needs_facts.meets: The record confirms type 2 diabetes during treatment.
A dated diagnosis or a pharmacist's answer confirms that diagnosed malnutrition was present during the GLP-1 course under review.

options.words: Diagnosed malnutrition was present during this treatment
Malnutrition was excluded during this treatment

needs_facts.meets: Type 2 diabetes was a reason for prescribing this GLP-1 analogue.

options.words: Prescribed for type 2 diabetes, alone or with another reason
